findings.area: scope / ADR-026 clause 1 (work worker subject substitution)
findings.summary: CLOSED: LibraryWorkWorker now keeps the item-id fallback as the subject and retains the bounded connection scope and image surface in both records; tests pin both components; WorkItemKey is unchanged.
findings.detail: DescribeWorkItem (src/ArrTags/Updates/LibraryWorkWorker.cs) returns `{LogSubject.Create(item.Key.ItemId)} ({item.Key.ConnectionId ?? "*"}, {surface})`, restoring the bounded connection scope and surface the pre-change WorkItemKey text carried while replacing only the item identifier (ADR-026 clause 1). LogProcessed and LogRetryScheduled both use it. WorkItemKey itself is not in the diff (coalescing identity unchanged). Tests: WorkWorkerSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity asserts `item <D> (*, Primary)` for the hint-derived key, and WorkWorkerRetrySubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity asserts `item <D> (radarr-connection-scope, Primary)` for a connection-scoped key, via AssertQueueContext. I re-checked every clause-3 site message pre/post change and no other non-subject bounded context (outcome/attempts/reason, provider kind/status/method, error code, discard reason, lifecycle sentence) was dropped.

findings.area: acceptance criteria / worker evidence (metadata-read-failure catch path)
findings.summary: CLOSED: a distinct reader-threw theory now drives the catch path (path-bearing and pathless) and asserts the subject; the claim is no longer overstated.
findings.detail: DriveMetadataReadFailureAsync gained a `readerThrows` switch: when set it assigns FakeMetadataReader.Handler to throw InvalidOperationException and leaves Result null, so FakeMetadataReader.ReadAsync (`Result ?? Handler(...)`) throws synchronously and the processor's catch block runs - genuinely the catch path, not the failed-read result. MetadataReaderThrowSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity asserts 'the reader threw InvalidOperationException.' plus AssertFileNameSubject, and MetadataReaderThrowSubjectFallsBackToTheItemIdWhenNoPathIsAvailable asserts the item-id fallback. The worker report acceptance_criteria[1] and the changelog now name both paths with their own theories.

findings.area: acceptance criteria / worker evidence (worker retry-scheduled path)
findings.summary: CLOSED: a retryable queue case now drives and asserts the WorkItemRetryScheduled record, including the retained connection/surface context.
findings.detail: DriveQueueRetryAsync enqueues a connection-scoped LibraryWorkItem with RetryableWorkItemProcessor, which returns WorkProcessingResult.Transient (IsRetryable == true for Retryability Later), so the worker reaches LogRetryScheduled before the bounded backoff. WorkWorkerRetrySubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity filters WorkItemRetryScheduled records, asserts AssertItemIdSubject on each, and pins AssertQueueContext with ConnectionScopeId + Primary. The computation is bounded (ComputeAttemptCount = TransientRetryCount + 1) and the test does not depend on the retry record count.
